curriculum_metadata.subject: Entrepreneurship Education
curriculum_metadata.source_document: ENTREPRENEURSHIP EDUCATION SYLLABUS ADVANCED SECONDARY CURRICULUM

values: Respect for humanity and the environment
Honesty, upholding and defending the truth at all times
Justice and fairness in dealing with others
Integrity; moral uprightness and sound character

themes.theme_description: Foundational concepts of entrepreneurship and the business environment.

topics.core_competency: The learner appreciates the role of entrepreneurship through the application of entrepreneurial skills and building a unique personal brand for the benefit of self and society.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: examine the role of entrepreneurship in economic development reflecting on the benefits and challenges of self-employment and paid employment in Uganda. (u, gs, v)
demonstrate entrepreneurial skills used in business operations. (s, gs, v)
create a unique personal brand; the importance of developing a personal brand; guidelines on personal branding for a selected business. (s, gs, v)
develop a unique personal brand for a selected business.

suggested_learning_activities.description: Learners brainstorm the: i) meaning of entrepreneurship. ii) role of entrepreneurship in the economic development of a country. Analyse real-world examples of entrepreneurs who have significantly contributed to economic development. They present their findings to the class for discussion.

In groups learners: i) read a case study on the benefits and challenges of self and paid employment with examples relevant to Uganda. ii) participate in a debating session, to discuss whether to opt for self or paid employment. Learners share their work with the class and take note of key points during the sessions.

In groups learners: a) use library resources and ICT tools to search and discuss entrepreneurial skills listed below showing how relevant each one is in business: i) Coping with change ii) Creativity skills iii) Innovation skills iv) Entrepreneurial motivation v) Communication skills vi) Negotiation skills b) Write an essay on the listed entrepreneurial skills and their relevance in business, and present it to the class for peer critiquing.

In groups learners: a) use guided discovery, to explore and discuss the: i) meaning of personal branding. ii) the importance of developing a personal brand. iii) guidelines on personal branding. iv) Present their work to the plenary.
Let learners display their work in class for a gallery walk and peer critiquing.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe the learners as they brainstorm to assess their ability to: i) use logical reasoning and develop ideas. ii) speak confidently and explain ideas clearly. iii) work independently with persistence iv) exhibit honesty, uphold and defend the truth at all times.

Engage learners in a dialogue, asking probing questions to assess their level of understanding of the role of entrepreneurship in economic development reflecting on the benefits and challenges of self employment and paid employment.
Assess the learners’ output of the case study analysis and make comments for improvement.

Observe learners as they search and discuss entrepreneurial skills, focusing on their ability to: i) use ICT to create, manipulate, and process information on entrepreneurial skills ii) work with others to generate ideas on the meaning and relevance of each skill in business iii) use imaginations to explore possibilities on the different entrepreneurial skills iv) talk confidently and explain opinions clearly
Converse with the learners while asking probing questions to assess their level of understanding of the different entrepreneurial skills.
Assess learners’ essays on entrepreneurial skills and how relevant they are in business, and give feedback for improvement.

Observe learners discuss the meaning, importance, and guidelines of personal branding, focusing on their ability to: i) take responsibility for their learning. ii) interact with each other. iii) talk confidently and explain ideas clearly. iv) exhibit honesty, and uphold and defend the truth at all times.
Converse with learners to assess their conceptualisation of personal branding.
Assess learners’ presentation of the meaning, importance, and guidelines of personal branding and make comments for improvement.

Observe learners develop a unique personal brand and assess their ability to: i) work with others to generate ideas. ii) use imaginations to explore possibilities. iii) speak confidently and explain opinions clearly. iv) demonstrate integrity, moral uprightness, and sound character.
Converse with learners while asking probing questions on their understanding of personal branding.
Assess learners’ unique personal brands and give feedback for improvement.

topics.core_competency: The learner analyses the political, economic, social, demographic, and global environment to undertake opportunities, and manage and sustain an enterprise for self and community benefit.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: examine the factors that influence different types; characteristics of entrepreneurial environments and organisations supporting Entrepreneurship in Uganda. (k, u, gs, v)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners: a) use textbook extracts on entrepreneurship and ICT resources to search and discuss the following: i) the meaning and types of entrepreneurial environments ii) characteristics of entrepreneurial environments. iii) organisations supporting Entrepreneurship in Uganda. Let them present the work to the plenary.

b) visit a nearby business community to establish the social, economic, political, and demographic factors that influence the start-up process, growth, and sustainability of a business. Let them prepare a report on the findings and present it to the class.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they discuss and present the meaning, types, characteristics and factors that influence the different types of entrepreneurial environments while focusing on their ability to: i) demonstrate ICT proficiency through searching their work ii) exhibit fluency and clarity. iii) interact effectively with others as they discuss iv) plan and carry out investigations v) exhibit respect for one another

In a conversation with learners, ask probing questions to assess their ability to evaluate different solutions as they present their work on the types, characteristics and organisations supporting entrepreneurship in Uganda.
Evaluate the learners’ output on the entrepreneurial environment and give feedback for improvement.

Observe learners as they interact with the business community to establish the social, economic, political, and demographic factors that influence the start-up process, growth, and sustainability of a business. Assess their ability to: i) interact with the. business community. ii) speak confidently and explain ideas clearly. iii) respect humanity and the environment.

Converse with learners while asking probing questions on the social, economic, political, and demographic factors that influence the start-up process, growth, and sustainability of a business, to assess their level of understanding of the above.
Assess learners’ field reports on social, economic, political, and demographic factors that influence the start-up process, growth, and sustainability of a business and make comments for improvement.

practicals.title: Community Business Visit
practicals.description_verbatim: visit a nearby business community to establish the social, economic, political, and demographic factors that influence the start-up process, growth, and sustainability of a business.

themes.theme_description: Scanning environment, planning business, and production processes.

topics.core_competency: The learner scans the environment, generates ideas, and selects viable business opportunities for self and community benefit.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: generate and evaluate business ideas from different sources. (s, gs, v)
evaluate and select a profitable business opportunity. (s, gs, v)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Learners in groups: a) discuss the reasons for generating business ideas and the factors considered when evaluating business ideas
b) visit a nearby community and conduct a transect walk to generate and evaluate profitable business ideas.
c) prepare a report about the findings and present it to the class.

In groups, learners: a) use library resources and ICT resources to search and discuss: i) the types of business opportunities ii) characteristics of a good business opportunity iii) procedures followed when evaluating the profitability of a potential business opportunity. iv) steps followed when turning a business idea into a business opportunity. Guide them to make a report on the findings and present it to the class.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they interact with the business community to generate business ideas. Assess their ability to: i) identify problems and ways forward. ii) interact effectively with others. iii) speak confidently and explain ideas clearly. iv) respect humanity and the environment.
Converse with learners and assess their understanding of the rationale for generating business ideas and the factors considered when evaluating business ideas.
Assess learners’ field reports on business ideas and make comments for improvement.

Observe learners as they search and discuss: i) the steps followed when turning a business idea into a business opportunity. ii) the types, characteristics of a good business opportunity, and procedures followed when evaluating the profitability of a potential business opportunity. Evaluate their ability to: i) sort and analyse information on the types, characteristics, and procedures followed when evaluating the profitability of a potential business opportunity. ii) develop ideas by considering different perspectives. iii) collaborate. iv) exhibit social responsibility.

In a conversation with learners, ask probing questions to assess the learners’ critical thinking skills on the types of business opportunities, characteristics of a good business, and steps followed when turning a business idea into a business opportunity.
Evaluate learners’ reports on the selection of a profitable business opportunity and give feedback for improvement.

practicals.title: Community Transect Walk
practicals.description_verbatim: visit a nearby community and conduct a transect walk to generate and evaluate profitable business ideas.

topics.core_competency: The learner follows the correct steps of preparing a business plan, and designs a workable business plan for the benefit of self and society.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: examine the rationale for writing a business plan, the steps followed when preparing a business plan, and the challenges for its implementation. (k, s, gs, v)
analyse the structure of a business plan. (k, s, gs, v)
prepare a workable business plan for a selected business. (s, gs, v)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners: a) use textbook and ICT resources on business planning to search and discuss the: i) meaning of a business plan. ii) rationale for writing a business plan. iii) steps followed when preparing a business plan. iv) challenges of implementing a business plan b) Present their work to the class for peer critiquing.

a. use the jigsaw method to search the following components of a business plan: i) executive summary ii) general description iii) production plan iv) marketing plan v) financial plan vi) human resource plan/ management plan vii) action plan Let them make a report on their findings and present it to the class.

In groups learners: a) use ICT devices and the internet to search for the structure of different business plans, and use them to prepare a business plan for a selected business. b) share their copies of business plans with other groups in class for peer critiquing.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they discuss and take note of how they: i) use technology to create, manipulate, and process information on business planning ii) work effectively in diverse teams iii) manage goals and time iv) write and present the rationale and steps followed when preparing a business plan. v) exhibit honesty, uphold and defend the truth at all times.

In a conversation with the learners, ask probing questions to assess their understanding of the meaning of a business plan, the rationale for preparing a business plan, and the challenges of implementing a business plan.
Evaluate the learners’ presentations and make comments for improvement.

Observe learners as they Jig saw and present the components of the business plan and take note of their: i) active participation ii) management of goals and time iii) self-expression iv) fluency and clarity v) ability to predict outcomes and make reasoned decisions vi) respect for humanity and the environment
Converse with learners while asking probing questions on the components of the business plan.
Evaluate the learners’ reports on the components of a business plan and comment for improvement.

Observe the learners as they design the business plans, and critique each other. Evaluate their ability to: i) sort and analyse information. ii) predict outcomes and make reasoned decisions. iii) work effectively in diverse teams. iv) suggest and develop new solutions. v) exhibit national consciousness and patriotism.
Converse with learners as they prepare business plans and assess their accuracy.
Evaluate learners on the designs of their business plan and give comments for improvement.

project_requirements.project_scope_verbatim: prepare a business plan for a selected business

topics.core_competency: The learner produces quality products by using appropriate inputs and technology to minimise production costs and satisfy customer needs in the community.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: examine the production process of a selected product and the factors affecting production decisions in a business. (u s, gs, v)
design and use relevant documents for purchasing business inputs and apply appropriate tools for inventory management in business. (s, gs, v)

examine the appropriate technology including i) the concept of technology, types of technology, ii) characteristics of appropriate technology, iii) factors that influence the choice of technology in business to be used by an enterprise. (u, gs, v)
examine quality management strategies including Mechanisms for controlling business assets, Ways of ensuring the production of quality products in business in a selected business. (s, gs, v)

apply effective time management skills in business covering the indicators of poor time management in business. i) advantages of good time management and disadvantages/costs of poor time management. ii) ways of ensuring effective time management in business. (s, gs, v)
estimate production costs for the requirements of producing a given product and suggest measures to minimise them in an enterprise. (s, gs, v)
Produce a quality product, use appropriate packaging material and design an appropriate label for an enterprise. (s, gs, v)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups learners: a) read textbook extracts on production in business or visit a local manufacturing business and discuss: i) the types of products produced by businesses ii) the production process of a selected product. iii) Factors affecting production decisions in business Have them make a presentation to the class on the production process and factors affecting production decisions in an enterprise

Learners: a) use library resources and the ICT tools to search and discuss the following: i) the concept of purchasing business requirements ii) factors to be considered when purchasing raw materials iii) steps to be followed in purchasing business goods and services iv) inventory management Task them to make a write-up on their findings and present it to the class.

a) Visit the nearby trading centre or school canteen to identify, record, and design documents used when purchasing business inputs. Let them display their work in class for gallery walks and peer critiquing.

a) In a guided group discussion, learners explore: i) the concept of technology. ii) types of technology. iii) characteristics of appropriate technology. iv) factors that influence the choice of technology in business. Task them to present their work to the class for peer critiquing.

a. Learners use think-pair-share to discuss: i) factors considered when selecting machinery, equipment, and tools for a business. ii) ways of ensuring proper machine use, maintenance, and handling in a business. Let them share their findings in a class discussion.

In groups learners: a) Learners use library resources and the ICT tools to search and discuss the following: i) Mechanisms for controlling business assets ii) Ways of ensuring the production of quality products in business Task them to present their work to the class for peer critiquing.

In groups learners: a) role-play the indicators of poor time management in business Take note of the indicators of poor time management. b) use guided discovery to explore and discuss the: i) advantages of good time management and disadvantages/costs of poor time management. ii) ways of ensuring effective time management in business. Let them display their work in class for a gallery walk and peer critiquing.

a) Using the inquiry-based method, learners: i) identify the production requirements and costs for a selected product and prepare a production budget. ii) suggest measures to minimise production costs. Let them present the findings to the class.

a) In groups learners: i) select and produce a quality product of their own choice. ii) identify the different types of packaging materials and select an appropriate one for their business product. iii) design a label to be used on the packaging material. Let them display their work in class for a gallery walk and peer critiquing.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they read and discuss the textbook extracts on the production process and factors affecting production decisions to assess how they: i) read accurately and fluently ii) sort and analyse information iii) develop ideas by considering different perspectives. iv) exhibit hard work for self-reliance
Converse with learners while asking probing questions to establish their understanding of the production process and factors affecting production decisions.
Evaluate learners’ presentations on the production process and factors affecting production decisions, and make comments for improvement.

Observe learners as they discuss. Evaluate their ability to: i) read accurately and fluently. ii) use technology to collaborate, communicate, and refine work. iii) work effectively in diverse teams. iv) exhibit integrity, moral uprightness, and sound character.
Converse with learners as they search for information to establish their mastery of purchasing skills and inventory management.
Evaluate learners’ write-up on purchasing business requirements and inventory management, and make comments for improvement.

Observe learners as they interact with the business community to identify the purchasing documents for a business. Assess their ability to: i) plan and carry out investigations. ii) interact effectively with others. iii) talk confidently and explain ideas clearly. iv) exhibit respect for humanity and the environment.
Evaluate the purchasing documents designed by learners and make comments for improvement.

Observe learners as they discuss and assess their ability to: i) use logical reasoning. ii) take responsibility for their learning. iii) talk confidently and explain ideas clearly. iv) exhibit respect for humanity and the environment.
Converse with learners while asking probing questions to assess their level of understanding of the different aspects of technology in business.
Assess learners’ output during the presentation and make comments for improvement.

In a conversation with learners, ask probing questions to assess their understanding of: i) factors considered when selecting machinery, equipment, and tools for the business. ii) ways of ensuring proper machine handling, use, and safety in a business.
Evaluate learners’ presentations and give comments for improvement.

Observe learners as they search and discuss mechanisms for controlling business assets and quality management in an enterprise, taking note of their ability to: i) read accurately and fluently. ii) take responsibility for their learning. iii) work independently with persistence. iv) exhibit respect for one another.
Converse with learners to assess their conceptualisation of mechanisms for controlling business assets and quality control in a business.
Evaluate learners’ presentations on mechanisms for controlling business assets and quality control in business, and give comments for improvement.

Observe learners as they role-play time management in business and assess their ability to: i) talk confidently and explain ideas clearly. ii) try out innovative alternatives during the role-play on time management. iii) take responsibility for their own learning. iv) work with others to generate ideas on effective time management in business. v) exhibit integrity, moral uprightness, and sound character.
Converse with learners while asking probing questions to evaluate their conceptualisation of effective time management during the role-play and discussion.
Assess learners’ role-play and discussion on effective time management in business and make comments for improvement.

Observe learners as they identify the requirements and costs of production for a selected product, and prepare a production budget. Assess their ability to exhibit: i) numerical strength when preparing a production budget. ii) integrity and honesty with costs.
Converse with learners while asking probing questions on production costs and the budget to establish integrity and honesty with costs.
Assess learners’ production budget and provide feedback for improvement.

Observe learners’ creative skills as they produce a quality product, design a unique label, use appropriate packaging materials for the product, and assess whether they: i) use imagination to explore and design an appropriate packaging material. ii) produce unique packaging material. iii) respect humanity and the environment.
Ask learners probing questions on how they are designing the label to be used on the packaging materials to trigger critical thinking.
Ask learners to comment on the labels and packaging materials of other groups and harmonise their comments.

practicals.title: Document Design Visit
practicals.description_verbatim: Visit the nearby trading centre or school canteen to identify, record, and design documents used when purchasing business inputs.

practicals.title: Product Production
practicals.description_verbatim: select and produce a quality product of their own choice. ii) identify the different types of packaging materials and select an appropriate one for their business product. iii) design a label to be used on the packaging material.

themes.theme_description: Marketing proficiency and social enterprise development.

topics.core_competency: The learner demonstrates proficiency in marketing products to customers by conducting thorough market research and utilising effective promotional strategies to maintain competitiveness in business.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: explore the components of a marketing mix; characteristics potential customers; market segmentation and creative selling process in an enterprise. (k, u, gs, v)
evaluate various sales promotion methods; types of advertising media and factors influencing the choice of the most effective medium of advertising used by the business community. (u, s, gs, v)
evaluate and select the most appropriate distribution channel considering the factors considered when selecting the appropriate distribution channel for selected business products. (s, gs, v)
develop a market survey tool and conduct market research to establish the customers of a selected product. (s, gs, v)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners: a) use think-pair-share to discuss the: i) meaning of marketing, target market population, marketing mix and factors determining the target market population ii) characteristics of potential customers iii) components of marketing mix Let them share the responses with the class and take note of the important aspects.

a) Learners use library resources and the ICT tools to search and discuss the following: i) meaning of market segmentation. ii) objectives of market segmentation. iii) basis of market segmentation. iv) meaning of creative selling and the process of creative selling. Guide them to write an essay on their findings and present to the class.

In groups, learners: a) conduct a field study in the business community to establish the: i) sales promotion methods used by the business community. ii) types of advertising media used by the business community. iii) factors influencing the choice of advertising media. Task them to prepare a report on their findings and present it to the class
b) Select a product and design an attractive advert to create awareness among the public and display them in class for a gallery walk and critiquing.

In groups learners: a) conduct a field study in the business community to establish the distribution channels used and factors that influence their selection. Make learners write a report about their findings on the distribution channels used and factors that influence their selection and present it to the class.
In groups, learners: a) use think-pair-share to discuss the meaning and tools of market research. Let learners present their responses to the class.

b) design a market research tool such as questionnaire or interview guide to use when collecting market information of a selected business. Task learners to display their designed market research tools in class for peer critiquing.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they discuss the concept of marketing, elements of marketing mix, target market population and the characteristics of potential customers while taking note of their ability to: i) interact with each other. ii) talk confidently and explain ideas clearly. iii) exhibit respect for humanity and the environment.
Converse with learners as they prepare their reports to assess their understanding of the target market population, marketing mix and characteristics of potential customers in the community.
Assess learners’ reports on the target market population, marketing mix and potential customers, give comments for improvement.

Observe learners discuss the meaning, objectives and basis of market segmentation and creative selling, taking note of their ability to: i) use ICT to search for work. ii) work effectively in diverse teams. iii) exhibit integrity, moral uprightness and sound character.
Converse with learners to establish their mastery of knowledge about market segmentation and creative selling
Evaluate learners’ essay on market segmentation and creative selling and make comments for improvement.

Observe learners as they interact with the business community to establish the sales promotion methods, advertising media and design attractive adverts for a selected product while taking note of their ability to: i) interact effectively with the business community. ii) listen attentively to the business community with comprehension. iii) exhibit respect for humanity and the environment. iv) use imaginations to explore and design attractive adverts for selected products. v) develop unique designs by considering different perspectives

Converse with the learners as they prepare their reports from the field to assess their understanding of the sales promotion methods, types of advertising media, factors influencing the choice of advertising media and the accuracy of their designed adverts
Assess learners’ outputs and make comments for improvement.

Observe learners as they interact with the business community to establish the distribution channels they use, take note of their ability to: i) work with others to generate ideas. ii) talk confidently and explain ideas. iii) demonstrate hard work for self-reliance.
Converse with the learners as they prepare their reports from the field to assess their understanding on the distribution channels used by the business community.
Assess learners’ field reports and comment for improvement.

Converse with learners as they discuss the meaning and tools of market research, develop a questionnaire or an interview guide on a selected product and evaluate the quality of: i) their questionnaires or interview guides. ii) their questions based on the 5Ps of marketing mix (product, price, promotion, place, people). iii) the information obtained from the target respondents in terms of relevance, accuracy and coherence.

Observe learners as they discuss the meaning and tools for market research and design a market research tool. Assess whether they: i) Work effectively with others to generate ideas. ii) Identify problems and propose appropriate solutions. iii) exhibit social harmony and engagement with the community.

Evaluate the learners’ output related to market research and provide feedback for improvement. Assessment should focus on the: i) clarity and relevance of the research tool design. ii) depth of analysis in identifying market research needs. iii) nature of feedback provided to peers during discussions.

practicals.title: Sales Promotion Field Study
practicals.description_verbatim: conduct a field study in the business community to establish the: i) sales promotion methods used by the business community. ii) types of advertising media used by the business community. iii) factors influencing the choice of advertising media.

practicals.title: Distribution Channel Field Study
practicals.description_verbatim: conduct a field study in the business community to establish the distribution channels used and factors that influence their selection.

topics.core_competency: The learner identifies social challenges within the community and develops innovative, sustainable enterprises that address these challenges, contributing to community development and environmental conservation.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: evaluate the characteristics; types and importance of social entrepreneurship; the steps followed to become a social entrepreneur; the negative (PEDVU) and positive (CHEWS) opportunities in the community. (u, gs, v)
evaluate the social enterprise plan; theory of change; the opportunity; the innovation; management and operations and sustainability in the community. (u, s, gs, v)
investigate the threats businesses have on the natural environment and the strategies taken to manage these environmental threats in the community. (u, gs, v)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners: a) read textbook and newspaper extracts on social entrepreneurship, and discuss the meaning, characteristics, types, importance, and steps followed to become a social entrepreneur. Let learners present their work in a plenary.
a) use think-pair-share to Identify negative opportunities (PEDVU) and positive opportunities (CHEWS) in the community. Make them present their findings to the class.
Learners: a) identify a social problem in the community and use the GEPIC structure to role-play how the problem can be solved.

a) use jigsaw method on the components of the social enterprise plan: i) introduction ii) theory of change iii) the opportunity iv) the innovation v) management and operations vi) sustainability vii) indicators of community and environmental impact assessment. Make learners present their work in class for peer critiquing.

a) in groups, Learners visit a nearby community to identify the negative effects of businesses on the natural environment and investigate the strategies businesses have implemented to manage these environmental threats. Task learners to compile a report based on their findings and present it to the class for discussion and feedback.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they discuss and analyse different aspects of social entrepreneurship. Assess their ability to: i) analyse the characteristics of social entrepreneurship. ii) exhibit respect for humanity and the environment.
In a conversation with learners, ask probing questions to assess their conceptualisation of the different aspects of social entrepreneurship.
Evaluate learners’ presentation on the different aspects of social entrepreneurship and give feedback for improvement.
In a conversation with learners, ask probing questions to assess their understanding of negative and positive opportunities and the structure of social enterprise plan.
Evaluate learners’ output on positive and negative opportunities and give feedback for improvement.

Observe learners as they role-play the GEPIC structure and assess their ability to: i) work effectively in diverse teams. ii) exhibit advocacy skills. iii) exhibit respect for humanity and the environment.
In a conversation with learners assess whether they can identify a social problem in the community and solve it using the GEPIC structure.
Assess learners as they role-play using the GEPIC structure to address a societal problem, providing constructive feedback to enhance their solutions and approach.

Observe learners as they Jig saw and present the components of the social enterprise plan. Assess their ability to: i) speak confidently and explain opinions clearly. ii) predict outcomes and make reasoned decisions. iii) work with others to generate ideas. iv) exhibit justice and fairness when dealing with others.
Converse with learners while asking probing questions to establish their conceptualisation of the components of a social enterprise plan and starting a social enterprise.
Evaluate learners’ output on the components of a social enterprise plan and make comments for improvement.

Observe learners as they interact with the community to assess the impact of businesses on the natural environment. Evaluate their ability to: i) exhibit respect of humanity and environment. ii) exhibit social responsibility to the community. iii) interact effectively with others. iv) identify environmental threats and generate strategies to manage them.
Converse with learners and assess their understanding of the negative effects of businesses to the natural environment and their solutions.
Assess the learners’ field report findings on the negative effects of businesses to the natural environment and their solutions. Give feedback for improvement.

practicals.title: Environmental Impact Field Visit
practicals.description_verbatim: visit a nearby community to identify the negative effects of businesses on the natural environment and investigate the strategies businesses have implemented to manage these environmental threats.
